summary: Reddit, X and Bluesky were unreachable today, so this is a thin, Hacker News-only report. Strongest themes: people fed up with ads on Android TV and fire-sticks, small businesses pushed to pay Meta just to reach their followers, and locale bugs in money inputs. Four ideas, each backed by multiple independent HN commenters.

ideas.title: One-Tap Ad-Free TV Setup
ideas.oneLiner: A phone app that wirelessly sets up an ad-free launcher and trims ad services on Android TV and Fire TV, no ADB knowledge needed.
ideas.problem: Android TV and Fire TV home screens push ads and promo banners, even inappropriate ones when kids are around. Power users fix it with a third-party launcher, sideloading and ADB, but that is fiddly, and on Fire sticks it is harder still. Non-technical owners are stuck with the ads.
ideas.targetUsers: Owners of Mi/Android TVs, Fire TV sticks and cheap TV boxes, including non-technical households that rely on a tech-savvy family member.
ideas.monetization: Free scan plus basic setup; one-time ₹299–₹499 unlock for the full profile (ad-service disabling, remote-button remap, per-device backup).
mvp: Pair with the TV over wireless debugging with a step-by-step guided flow
One-tap install and default-set of a chosen ad-free launcher
Disable a curated, reversible list of promo and recommendation packages
Remap OEM remote shortcut buttons
Undo / restore-defaults button and a saved profile per device

competitors.name: Projectivy Launcher
competitors.gap: Great launcher, but users must find it, sideload it and set it as default themselves; it does not reach the ad services.

competitors.name: FLauncher / ATV Launcher Pro
competitors.gap: Same DIY setup; commenters note Fire sticks make launcher replacement much harder.

sources.title: An ad-free Android TV (HN thread)
sources.quote: It's much harder to switch out the launcher on a FireStick, but I did manage it briefly before it started boot looping right around 1yr of ownership, so it's e-waste now.

sources.title: An ad-free Android TV (HN thread)
sources.quote: At least Google lets me install Projectivy Launcher on the device I paid for so I never have to see a single ad on my TV. And use ADB to customize those branded OEM remote buttons for HBO/Netflix/etc to do what I want instead.

sources.title: An ad-free Android TV (HN thread)
sources.quote: Sucks, because Android TV still has some of the best flexibility in a TV-appropriate OS (compared with other options I could find at least) but their priorities don't line up with mine regarding the ads.

sources.title: An ad-free Android TV (HN thread)
sources.quote: Do you have a suggestion for an alternative to an Apple TV which includes your criteria? That is, good interface, no ads.

ideas.title: Closing-Early Page for Local Shops
ideas.oneLiner: A dead-simple page and QR code where a small shop posts hours, specials and 'closing early today', pushed to WhatsApp and Google listings.
ideas.problem: Small businesses use Facebook Pages for hours, events and closing-early notices because a website feels like a cost and a chore. Facebook now charges to post links and demotes page content, while customers who avoid Meta can't find basic info.
ideas.targetUsers: Cafes, salons, tailors, clinics and kirana-style shops with no website; their customers who want hours without a Facebook login.
ideas.monetization: Free page with branding; ₹199–₹399/month for custom domain, WhatsApp broadcast and Google Business Profile sync.
mvp: Phone-first editor: hours, holiday closures, today's special, menu photo
One-tap 'closing early' banner with auto-expiry
Free subdomain plus printable QR poster
Share to WhatsApp status/broadcast and copy for Instagram
Optional Google Business Profile hours sync

competitors.name: Squarespace / Wix
competitors.gap: Commenters say a template takes 2–3 hours even for non-technical owners, and the monthly fee and editing effort still deter tiny shops.

competitors.name: Google Business Profile
competitors.gap: Handles hours but not specials, menus or follower notifications, and many owners never claim it.

sources.title: Facebook Pages require paid subscription to post more than two links per month (HN thread)
sources.quote: There needs to be an easy to use low-cost, possible also advertisement driven, alternative that business can latch to so more can leave facebook.

sources.title: Facebook Pages require paid subscription to post more than two links per month (HN thread)
sources.quote: I still remember when Facebook Pages were promoted as an alternative to feeds and newsletters. You could follow a page and be sure to receive all updates from them. Now you even have to pay to share links.

sources.title: Facebook Pages require paid subscription to post more than two links per month (HN thread)
sources.quote: Why is there no GUI desktop app that lets you easily make a website?

sources.title: Facebook Pages require paid subscription to post more than two links per month (HN thread)
sources.quote: Anymore, putting up a basic template page for your business is maybe 2-3 hours if you're really non-technical.

ideas.title: Locale-Safe Money Input Guard
ideas.oneLiner: A tiny drop-in component and lint rule that parses and confirms currency amounts correctly across comma, dot and lakh-style locales.
ideas.problem: Typing 5,04 gets read as 504.00 on a payment screen, and users report the same bug when selling on marketplaces. It causes real overcharges and slow support disputes.
ideas.targetUsers: Indie developers and small teams building checkout, top-up or invoicing forms for international or Indian audiences.
ideas.monetization: Open-source core; paid ₹1,500–₹4,000 one-time licence for the React/Flutter widgets and lint pack, or GitHub sponsors.
mvp: Parser that detects ambiguous input such as 5,04 versus 5.04
Confirm-in-words step ('five dollars and four cents') before charging
React and Flutter input widgets
Lakh/crore and European format test suite
ESLint rule flagging parseFloat on money fields

competitors.name: Intl.NumberFormat / currency.js / Dinero.js
competitors.gap: Format and calculate well but do not guard the raw user-typed string or warn on ambiguous separators.

sources.title: Anthropic Console overcharged my card 100x due to internationalization input bug (HN thread)
sources.quote: I'm looking at the "Add credits" screen on https://platform.claude.com and it prominently displays the "total due" as $504.00 when typing `5,04` into the input...

sources.title: Anthropic Console overcharged my card 100x due to internationalization input bug (HN thread)
sources.quote: This happens everywhere . I'm in Germany (which uses commas) but have my distro set to English (using dots). I've encountered this problem on many sites, eg Amazon or eBay where I accidentally sell my items for 599,00 instead of 5.99

ideas.title: Chat-Based Dead Man's Switch
ideas.oneLiner: A Telegram/WhatsApp bot that checks in on you and releases messages to chosen people in escalating steps if you go silent.
ideas.problem: Solo operators and freelancers want a failsafe that tells clients or family where credentials live if something happens. Existing options are tied to one ecosystem, run only on rigid schedules, or require self-hosting and a weekly manual check-in people fear missing.
ideas.targetUsers: Solo developers, freelancers and small-business owners who hold the only keys to servers, domains and accounts.
ideas.monetization: Free for one contact; ₹149–₹299/month for multiple recipients, staged messages and passive signals.
mvp: Plain-language setup in chat: message, recipient, silence threshold
Escalating reminders before anything is released
Configurable check-in cadence
Passive check-in from phone activity or wearable data
Recipient confirmation and yearly rehearsal reminder

competitors.name: Google Inactive Account Manager
competitors.gap: Only covers Google data and checks in roughly quarterly.

competitors.name: Death Plan Switch (self-hosted)
competitors.gap: Fixed weekly email check-in and requires self-hosting.
